transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 min
Attendees: Marina Patel (Redwood AE), Devon Liu (Redwood SE), Tomás Rivera (CTO, Aegis), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Aegis), Leo Kim (Infra Lead, Aegis)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Aegis Robotics is scoping an inference pilot to decide between hosted, dedicated, or private deployment. Key success criteria: latency P95 <200ms for short prompts, 500 rps burst handling for fleet telemetry, cost target <$0.0009 per token (aspirational), and SOC2+KMS. Redwood to propose a 2-week benchmarking sprint followed by a 4-week pilot.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, security/compliance, routing/fallback strategy, rollouts

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Marina (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Marina, AE on the inference team, and Devon here is our SE who will run the bench sprint.
[00:12] Tomás (CTO): Hi all, Tomás here. Thanks for fitting us in. we've got three people from our side, Priya and Leo, both on.
[00:18] Priya (Head of ML): Hey. quick note, we run models for fleet telemetry summarization and agent instruction generation. mostly short prompts, many short context windows, but occasionally longer state reconstructions.
[00:30] Devon (SE): Great, thanks. can you say approximate QPS and token counts? even ballpark helps sizing.
[00:37] Priya: Sure — baseline is about 250 QPS during working hours, spikes to 500 for a few minutes when we wake a batch of robots. tokens per request: median 120 tokens, p95 400.
[00:50] Leo (Infra): We also have strict data residency rules for EU customers and some IP that cannot leave our VPC.
[00:58] Marina: OK — good flags. from Redwood's standpoint the main tradeoffs are: hosted gives fastest ramp, dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and cost, private is for full network isolation and strict KMS control.
[01:12] Tomás: We're leaning to minimize ops but also can't leak IP. so not sure. also curious about tail latency and cost delta.
[01:18] Devon: Understood. first pass, for your workload we suggest a benchmark sprint: 2 weeks where we run identical traffic on hosted and on a dedicated small pool. we measure P50/P95/P99, cold-start behavior, KV-cache hit rate, and cost per token.
[01:34] Priya: When you say KV-cache hit rate you mean prefix caching / session caching, right?
[01:37] Devon: Yes, prefix caching and shared KV for repeated context sequences. sometimes transcripts say KV cash in our docs — ignore that typo.
[01:45] Priya: haha, good to know.
[01:48] [00:60] (sic) Marina: Our typical pilot flow: week 0 - prep and data ingest; weeks 1-2 - bench sprint and perf tuning; weeks 3-6 - pilot with traffic mirroring and canary; acceptance criteria finalized at week 6. but we can compress if needed.
[02:04] Tomás: Timeline matters — we want a decision within one month. is that realistic?
[02:10] Devon: One month is tight but doable if you can give sample traces and we run parallel hosted + dedicated microbenchmarks. private will need more setup (VPN/VPC peering, KMS integration), likely 3-6 weeks.
[02:22] Leo: For private, our security team insists on HSM-backed KMS and audit trails. can Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:31] Marina: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integrations and provide audit logs. for Dedicated we offer encryption at rest with managed KMS, and hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but can support bring-your-own KMS in select enterprise plans.
[02:48] Priya: Cool. about SLOs — we need 99.9% availability and p95 latency under 200ms for 90% of calls. is that realistic?
[02:57] Devon: 99.9% is typical for dedicated with SLA; hosted regionally can meet that too depending on plan. p95 <200ms depends heavily on model choice and sequence lengths — with short prompts and caching we can get there, but for longer contexts you see higher tail.
[03:15] Priya: Our model ops team is also considering quantized variants to save cost, but we don't want quality regressions. can Redwood help recommend quantization profiles?
[03:24] Marina: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching profiles tuned to your workload, and our SEs can run evals against your prompt set to measure quality delta.
[03:34] Tomás: What kind of cost delta between hosted and dedicated? give me a ballpark for our scale.
[03:39] Devon: Ballpark: hosted is easiest but often 10-30% higher unit cost than dedicated at steady-state, because dedicated amortizes GPU pools. private tends to be similar to dedicated in unit cost but adds infra overhead. exacts depend on your batchability and cache hit rates.
[03:54] Priya: We're sensitive to per-token cost — target is under $0.0009 but that's aspirational.
[04:00] Marina: We'll run an initial cost model and include scenarios — optimistic (good cache hit, high batching), conservative (low cache hit), and realistic.
[04:10] [04:15] Speaker 1 (perhaps auto-label): question about fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is overloaded, what's the fallback?
[04:20] Devon: We support smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants or hosted pool depending on policy. you can set policies to favor low-latency vs low-cost.
[04:31] Leo: What about audits and log retention? our compliance team wants 12 months of immutable audit logs and ability to export logs to our SIEM.
[04:41] Marina: That is supported on Private and Dedicated with add-on retention; hosted supports exporting to your SIEM but retention policies vary by plan. we can include a compliance addon in the proposal.
[04:55] Priya: For benchmarks, what artifacts will Redwood need from us?
[05:00] Devon: We'll need representative request traces, token length distribution, a small prompt set (50-200 prompts) for quality checks, and any PII redaction rules. also network topology details for private.
[05:13] Priya: We'll prepare that.
[05:16] Tomás: How do you handle model versioning and rollbacks? important for production.
[05:20] Marina: Redwood Console supports pinning model versions, canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous version on regression. we also have differential evals to catch quality regressions.
[05:31] [05:40] Priya: Is there a performance guide for batching and target latency tradeoffs?
[05:44] Devon: yes, we'll share our batching heuristics doc — key point is latency vs cost: larger batch sizes reduce cost but increase tail latency; our runtime supports continuous batching to smooth that tradeoff.
[05:55] Tomás: Any gotchas for robotic telemetry? we sometimes have a lot of short synchronous calls that can't be batched.
[06:02] Devon: For synchronous short calls, KV caching and prefix reuse is your best ally. also consider micro-batching at the client side or a short-lived aggregator before calling the model.
[06:12] Leo: Network egress — if we use hosted, does data leave our VPC? yes — hosted is Redwood's multi-tenant service. can we VPC peering to hosted?
[06:22] Marina: Hosted is multi-tenant; we have region isolation, but it won't live inside your VPC. for private we deploy inside your VPC or on-prem. dedicated offers reserved capacity but still runs in Redwood-managed network unless you opt for private connectivity options — we can discuss private link or peering options.
[06:40] Priya: Quality checks — can you run comparative evals between quantized model and baseline?
[06:45] Devon: Absolutely — we run automated evals and custom prompt sets. we'll surface regressions with examples and scoring.
[06:51] Marina: Let's talk acceptance criteria so we have a clear go/no-go. Priya — can you propose a short list?
[06:57] Priya: Sure. 1) P95 latency <200ms for 80% of production requests; 2) P99 below 500ms for 95% of requests; 3) End-to-end cost per request below $0.12 (based on median tokens); 4) No more than 2% model quality regression vs baseline on our eval prompts; 5) Security: SOC2 or equivalent + customer KMS for private or dedicated.
[07:18] Marina: Good list. We'll map those to measurable benchmarks and include thresholds in the pilot proposal.
[07:24] Tomás: On timeline again — if we push for decision in 4 weeks, can you run hosted + dedicated bench sprint in parallel?
[07:30] Devon: Yes, we can kick off parallel runs; private would be out-of-scope for a 4-week decision unless your infra team can provision VPC peering fast.
[07:40] Leo: Our infra can move quickly but HSM provisioning might add time.
[07:45] Marina: We'll note that.
[07:47] [08:00] (time markers become approximate) Devon: For the benchmark plan: week 1 = synthetic load tests to validate throughput and latency; week 2 = replay of real traces (you supply) and quality checks. we'll run side-by-side hosted vs dedicated and produce a spreadsheet with P50/P95/P99, cost per token, cache hit rates, and guidance on batching/quant.
[08:20] Priya: OK. what about instrumentation hooks — can we get token-level cost breakdowns and traces?
[08:25] Marina: Redwood Console gives token-level traces, per-route cost, latency breakdowns, and we can integrate tracing headers to link calls to your traces.
[08:35] Tomás: If we do dedicated, what's a sensible initial capacity?
[08:39] Devon: For 250 steady QPS and 500 spikes, we recommend starting with a small dedicated pool of 2-3 GPUs (model-dependent), with autoscale configured. we'll refine after bench numbers.
[08:52] Priya: Any recommendations on model size? we run distillations and medium LLMs today.
[08:58] Devon: Smaller models reduce latency and cost; if quality meets your need, great. otherwise consider mixing: high-quality model for long-context aggregation and smaller, faster model for telemetry. Redwood supports hybrid routing.
[09:12] Leo: Misc question — how do you handle data retention and deletion requests?
[09:17] Marina: We have APIs for data deletion and configurable retention windows. for private, you control retention fully. for hosted, we can set retention limits per agreement.
[09:26] Priya: Great.
[09:28] Tomás: Let's close with concrete next steps.
[09:31] Marina: Recap: Redwood will send pilot proposal + cost scenarios and benchmarking plan by Friday 2027-03-05. Devon shares benchmark spreadsheet and runbook. Customer will send sample traces and prompt set by 2027-03-04. We'll schedule a pilot kickoff demo 2027-03-09 for 30 minutes.
[09:49] Priya: Sounds good.
[09:50] Leo: We'll get infra details to you — network topology and HSM constraints.
[09:55] Marina: Any other questions?
[09:56] Priya: One quick one — for peak spikes, can you support burst capacity without dedicated pool?
[09:59] Devon: Hosted can absorb burst but costs more; dedicated can be configured with burst credits or autoscale. we can design hybrid fallback to hosted for infrequent spikes.
[10:12] Tomás: Thanks everyone.
[10:14] Marina: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs.
